title: Eight Billion of Us
sourceTitle: UN World Population Prospects 2024 and other public data (data-journalism short)

scenes.title: One Dot
scenes.narration: This dot is one person. Zoom out: 100 people, 10,000, a million. On to 8 billion and more: humanity today.

props.todayNote: Disc drawn for 8 billion; ≈8.2 billion in 2024 (UN, World Population Prospects 2024)
props.credit: Data: UN Population Division, World Population Prospects 2024 and more · Visuals: all drawn live in code

props.title: Eight Billion of Us
props.subtitle: From one dot to eight billion dots
props.source: Data: UN Population Division, World Population Prospects 2024 and more; sources itemized in the notes

scenes.title: An Almost Flat Line
scenes.narration: In AD 1, Earth had about 300 million people. By 1500, still only about 500 million. Then the line shot straight up.

props.title: 1,800 years of an almost flat line
props.note: Billions of people; y-axis drawn to true scale
props.source: Source: UN Population Division, The World at Six Billion (1999), table 1; from 1950, World Population Prospects 2024 mid-year estimates

scenes.title: The First Billion
scenes.narration: Another view: each dot is a million people. Around 1804, we first reached 1 billion.

props.source: Source: UN Population Division, The World at Six Billion (1999), table 1 and box 3; dot counts interpolated by year

scenes.title: Years per Billion
scenes.narration: The second billion took 123 years. The third, 33 years. The fourth, just 14 years. Then 13 years, 12, and 12 again. The UN marked 8 billion on November 15, 2022. This time, it took just 11 years.

props.title: How many years it took
props.note: Each bar stands at the year that billion was reached; height = years since the previous billion
props.source: Sources: UN Population Division, The World at Six Billion (1999), box 3; UNFPA (2011, 7 billion); UN (2022, 8 billion)

scenes.title: Deaths Fell First
scenes.narration: It's mainly fewer deaths, not more births. Vaccines and antibiotics saved more children. Clean water helped them grow up, too. Fertilizer and better seeds fed the growth.

props.title: Deaths fell first, births later
props.note: Demographic transition, schematic (shape only, not measured data)
props.source: Basis: UN World Population Prospects 2024 summary, box I.2 “Why do populations peak?” (demographic transition schematic)

scenes.title: The Growth Rate Peaked
scenes.narration: But the turn came long ago. Global growth peaked in 1963, at about 2.3%. It has fallen since, to under 1% today.

props.title: Global population growth rate
props.source: Source: UN World Population Prospects 2024 annual growth rate (via Our World in Data)

scenes.title: An Aging World
scenes.narration: Fewer kids, longer lives: the world is aging. By the late 2070s, the balance tips. People 65+ will outnumber those under 18.

props.title: Soon, more elders than children
props.note: Billions of people; UN median projection after 2024
props.source: Source: UN World Population Prospects 2024, key messages 3, 5, 8; age groups via Our World in Data; under-18s estimated by splitting the 15–24 group evenly

scenes.title: India Overtakes China
scenes.narration: India overtook China around 2023, per the UN. China's population is already shrinking.

props.title: India overtakes China
props.note: Billions of people; UN median projection after 2024
props.crossNote: Each about 1.43 billion; the exact date is an estimate
props.source: Source: UN World Population Prospects 2024 mid-year population; UN DESA Policy Brief No. 153 (2023); the crossover date varies slightly by revision

scenes.title: Peak and Uncertainty
scenes.narration: The UN's median projection points to a peak. About 10.3 billion, in the mid-2080s. Then a slow decline. But the future is uncertain. The 95% range for 2100 is wide. It runs from 9 to 11.4 billion.

props.title: Will it keep rising?
props.note: Billions of people; UN median projection and 95% interval
props.odds: Chance of peaking this century: about 80%
props.fanNote: Mid-years of the fan are schematic; the 2100 ends are UN values
props.source: Source: UN World Population Prospects 2024: Summary of Results, pp. 8 and 41; 1950–2023 are estimates

scenes.title: One in Eight Billion
scenes.narration: Over 8 billion, one person at a time. And you are one of them.

props.todayNote: Disc drawn for 8 billion; ≈8.2 billion in 2024 (UN, World Population Prospects 2024)
